text: What distinguishes an ideal I of a ring R from a mere subring?
choices: Absorption: rI ⊆ I and Ir ⊆ I for every r ∈ R
Closure of I under multiplication of its own elements
explanation: An ideal must swallow multiplication by ARBITRARY ring elements, not just its own — that is exactly what makes the quotient multiplication (r+I)(s+I) = rs+I well defined. An ideal containing 1 would absorb everything and be all of R.
